qt: to the Commission Konstantinos Arvanitis (The Left) Subject:

According to witness statements and news reports1, on the afternoon of 4 April around 100 migrants and/or refugees were held at gunpoint on the deck of a so-called Libyan ‘coastguard’ vessel in international waters in the Mediterranean Sea, 95 miles off the coast of Libya. Many of those on board risked their lives by jumping into the sea to escape inhumane treatment. The Mediterranea Saving Humans rescue ship, which was sailing nearby, managed to rescue 58 people. The audiovisual material2appears to show members of the so-called Libyan ‘coastguard’ shooting at the rescue ship during the rescue operation, posing a direct threat to the lives of those being rescued as well as to the rescuers. After disembarkation at Pozzallo, Sicily, an order was issued for the temporary seizure of the vessel on the grounds of an alleged violation of Article (f) of Italian Law No 15/2023. In light of all the relevant reports3 and complaints about crimes against humanity and violations of the fundamental human rights of refugees and migrants by the so-called Libyan ‘coastguard’, can the Commission answer the following: 1.

Does it plan to go on supporting the so-called Libyan ‘coastguard’ through the EU-Libya agreement despite being aware of constant gross human rights violations and of the fact that the ‘coastguard’ is posing a threat to people’s lives and physical integrity?
What does it intend to do to protect the lives of those carrying out search and rescue operations in international waters?
at: (English version) to the Commission Konstantinos Arvanitis (The Left) (8 April 2024) Subject: Question regarding Libyan ‘coastguard’ attack against rescue ship According to witness statements and news reports (1), on the afternoon of 4 April around 100 migrants and/or refugees were held at gunpoint on the deck of a so-called Libyan ‘coastguard’ vessel in international waters in the Mediterranean Sea, 95 miles off the coast of Libya. Many of those on board risked their lives by jumping into the sea to escape inhumane treatment. The Mediterranea Saving Humans rescue ship, which was sailing nearby, managed to rescue 58 people. The audiovisual material (2)appears to show members of the so-called Libyan ‘coastguard’ shooting at the rescue ship during the rescue operation, posing a direct threat to the lives of those being rescued as well as to the rescuers. After disembarkation at Pozzallo, Sicily, an order was issued for the temporary seizure of the vessel on the grounds of an alleged violation of Article (f) of Italian Law No 15/2023. In light of all the relevant reports (3) and complaints about crimes against humanity and violations of the fundamental human rights of refugees and migrants by the so-called Libyan ‘coastguard’, can the Commission answer the following: 1.

Does it plan to go on supporting the so-called Libyan ‘coastguard’ through the EU-Libya agreement despite being aware of constant gross human rights violations and of the fact that the ‘coastguard’ is posing a threat to people’s lives and physical integrity?
What does it intend to do to protect the lives of those carrying out search and rescue operations in international waters?

(20 June 2024) The primary objective of the EU support to the Libyan coast guard authorities is to strengthen their capacities to carry out effective search and rescue (SAR) operations in full respect of international law and human rights, and in line with European Council’s mandate, through the provision of equipment and training and the provision of expertise for the development of standard operating procedures (SOPs), in close cooperation with Member States and international organisations. It is important to continue our engagement with relevant Libyan actors, working closely with Member States and other international partners, including United Nations agencies. It is the only way to improve existing conditions, provide lifesaving humanitarian activities and ensure search and rescue operations. So far, over 200 officers benefitted from training via the Support to Integrated border and migration management in Libya (SIBMMIL) programme (4). All trainings have a module on human rights and international maritime law. Such trainings will be continued and strengthened in cooperation with implementing partners involved in the SIBMMIL programme and other ongoing EU programmes in this policy area. In parallel, the EU has been continuously advocating for the set-up of a comprehensive governance and management system and search and rescue operations in full respect of international law and human rights.
